title: A dimension-free directed \(\mathrm{L}^{1}\) Poincaré inequality
formal: Does there exist an absolute constant \(C<\infty\) such that, for every integer \(n\ge 1\) and every Lipschitz function \(f:[0,1]^{n}\to \mathbb{R} , d_{1}^{\mathrm{mono}}(f) \le  C \int _{[0,1]^{n}} (\sum_{i=1}^{n} \max \{- \partial _{i}f(x),0\}^{2})^{1/2} dx\)? Here \(d_{1}^{\mathrm{mono}}(f)\) is the \(\mathrm{L}^{1}\) distance to the coordinatewise nondecreasing functions. The same C must work for every dimension and every finite Lipschitz constant.
context:
A negative partial derivative witnesses a local decrease in one coordinate. The left-hand side measures the least average change to the entire function needed to remove all monotonicity violations.

The 2023 source proves a directed inequality using \(E\Vert \nabla ^{-}f\Vert _{1}\). Comparing \(\ell\)\(_{1}\) and \(\ell\)\(_{2}\) norms yields a bound with a factor \(\sqrt{n}\), whereas the conjecture asks to remove all dependence on dimension.

The later theorem bounds squared \(\mathrm{L}^{2}\) distance to monotonicity by \(C\cdot E\Vert \nabla ^{-}f\Vert _{2}^{2}\). Even though \(\mathrm{L}^{2}\) distance dominates \(\mathrm{L}^{1}\) distance, the square root of this second moment can be much larger than \(E\Vert \nabla ^{-}f\Vert _{2}\). The author explicitly leaves the present conjecture open.

The 2025 thesis restates the inequality after obtaining a tester with sublinear dimension dependence from the \(\mathrm{L}^{2}\) theorem. Thus the motivating algorithmic progress and the analytic conjecture have distinct statuses.
why: Would connect local directional decreases to global distance from monotonicity with a universal constant, extending a central isoperimetric principle to real-valued functions on continuous cubes.
status_note: The full 2023 conjecture, October 2024 preprint revision and July 2025 thesis were checked, including the explicit statement that the later norm inequality does not resolve this one. Searches through 12 September 2026 located no resolution of the full continuous-cube claim.

progress.text: The directed \((\mathrm{L}^{1},\ell _{1})\) inequality is proved; the dimension-free \((\mathrm{L}^{1},\ell _{2})\) version is Conjecture 1.8.
The directed \((\mathrm{L}^{2},\ell _{2})\) theorem yields improved testing bounds but explicitly does not settle this conjecture.
The thesis retains the same statement as Conjecture 4.43.

sentences: The conjecture concerns every Lipschitz real-valued function on a continuous unit cube.
It asks whether average distance to a monotone function is controlled by the average Euclidean magnitude of the negative gradient.
The multiplicative constant must be independent of the dimension and the Lipschitz constant.
A known inequality using the sum of coordinate decreases loses a square-root dimension factor.
Later work proves a different inequality using squared quantities and explicitly leaves this conjecture open.

references.title: Directed Poincaré Inequalities and L¹ Monotonicity Testing of Lipschitz Functions

definitions:
Lebesgue measure on \([0,1]^{n}\) has total mass one. A function \(g:[0,1]^{n}	o \mathbb{R}\) is coordinatewise nondecreasing if \(g(x)\le g(y)\) whenever \(x_{i}\le y_{i}\) for all i. Define \(d_{1}^{\mathrm{mono}}(f)=\inf _{g} \int |f(x)- g(x)|dx\), over measurable integrable coordinatewise nondecreasing g; g need not have the same Lipschitz constant as f. A function f is Lipschitz if there is a finite L with |\(f(x)- f(y)|\le \mathrm{L}\Vert x- y\Vert _{2}\) for all x,y in the cube. Its gradient exists almost everywhere; its values on the exceptional null set may be set to zero without changing any integral. The negative gradient is \(
abla ^{-}f(x)=(\max \{- \partial _{1}f(x),0\},\ldots ,\max \{- \partial _{n}f(x),0\})\). The right-hand side is \(C\cdot E[\Vert 
abla ^{-}f(X)\Vert _{2}]\) for a uniform point X in the cube. It is not \(C\cdot (E[\Vert 
abla ^{-}f(X)\Vert _{2}^{2}])^{1/2}\). No boundary condition, mean-zero assumption or fixed bound on the range of f is imposed.
answer_criterion: Prove the displayed inequality with one universal finite C, or refute the existence of such a C by showing that the ratio \(d_{1}^{\mathrm{mono}}(f)/E\Vert \nabla ^{-}f\Vert _{2}\) is unbounded across the stated functions and dimensions (including a function with positive distance and zero denominator, if one existed). A bound whose constant grows with n, or a bound using the \(\mathrm{L}^{2}\) norm of the gradient over the cube, is insufficient.
